questions.stem: The record name is web and its private zone is clz.internal. Which name does that create?

options.A: web.clz.internal
options.B: clz.internal.web
options.C: web.internal.clz

optionExplanations.A: A relative record name combines with the zone name to form the FQDN.
optionExplanations.B: That reverses the DNS label order.
optionExplanations.C: That is a different name from the declared zone and record.
optionExplanations.D: The record's IPv4 value is not appended as a DNS suffix.

questions.stem: Which address is configured for web.clz.internal in CLZ-290?

options.B: The NAT public IP from CLZ-280 automatically
options.C: The first public IP created by every prior lesson
options.D: The entire 10.40.0.0/16 prefix

optionExplanations.A: The Terraform A record contains that teaching-only private IPv4.
optionExplanations.B: The separate configuration declares a literal private address.
optionExplanations.C: Prior lessons are not implicitly queried by this record.
optionExplanations.D: An A record contains individual IPv4 addresses, not a subnet prefix.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish a DNS record from a workload
questions.stem: The name resolves to 10.40.1.10 but no web service responds. Why is that expected in the unmodified lesson?

options.A: Private DNS always blocks HTTP even when a VM exists
options.B: The A record installs only Linux applications
options.C: The zone requires an administrator password for HTTP resolution
options.D: No VM or application is created at the illustrative record address

optionExplanations.A: DNS does not itself block application ports.
optionExplanations.B: An A record does not install any application.
optionExplanations.C: The lesson does not use guest authentication to resolve this name.
optionExplanations.D: DNS data can exist without a running endpoint at its value.

questions.stem: What does the zone's virtual network link provide?

options.A: A public Internet delegation for clz.internal
options.B: Resolution scope for the private zone from the linked VNet
options.C: An inbound RDP rule for all VMs
options.D: A VM image containing the lesson page

optionExplanations.A: A private VNet link is not public DNS delegation.
optionExplanations.B: The relationship makes the zone available through the appropriate resolver path.
optionExplanations.C: DNS linkage does not open guest management ports.
optionExplanations.D: The link is DNS configuration, not an image resource.

questions.stem: registration_enabled is false in CLZ-290. What is the intended consequence?

options.A: The linked VNet cannot resolve any private records
options.B: The zone is automatically deleted after one query
options.C: The link does not automatically create VM hostname records
options.D: Every DNS response becomes a public IP

optionExplanations.A: Resolution links can work without autoregistration.
optionExplanations.B: Autoregistration is not a lifetime timer.
optionExplanations.C: The declared web A record is managed explicitly by Terraform.
optionExplanations.D: Registration setting does not translate addresses.

questions.stem: Where should Resolve-DnsName web.clz.internal be run for the stated data-plane test?

options.A: On any Internet laptop with no VPN or resolver connection
options.B: On a client in the linked VNet using an appropriate Azure DNS resolver path
options.C: Only inside the Terraform provider's source repository
options.D: On the GitHub Pages hosting server automatically

optionExplanations.A: That laptop lacks the intended private DNS path.
optionExplanations.B: The client needs access to the private resolution scope.
optionExplanations.C: The repository location is unrelated to live DNS resolution.
optionExplanations.D: The static site does not join the Azure VNet.

questions.stem: Azure CLI shows the A record's value. What does that alone prove?

options.A: The record exists in Azure control-plane configuration
options.B: Every on-premises client can resolve the private name
options.C: The target address runs a healthy IIS service
options.D: The zone's public registrar delegation is correct

optionExplanations.A: A separate client query is needed to demonstrate actual resolver behavior.
optionExplanations.B: Configuration listing does not verify hybrid forwarding.
optionExplanations.C: No endpoint test has occurred.
optionExplanations.D: This private zone does not rely on public delegation.

questions.stem: A VM is in the linked VNet but uses custom DNS servers that do not forward clz.internal. What should be reviewed?

options.A: Only the VM's local administrator username
options.B: Only the load balancer's frontend port
options.C: Conditional forwarding or an appropriate Azure DNS Private Resolver design
options.D: Only the browser's saved quiz percentage

optionExplanations.A: Guest usernames do not configure DNS forwarding.
optionExplanations.B: The lesson creates no load balancer for private name resolution.
optionExplanations.C: The custom resolver needs a route for the private namespace.
optionExplanations.D: Learning progress has no effect on DNS servers.

questions.stem: Does creating web.clz.internal automatically create a route or permit application traffic to 10.40.1.10?

options.A: Yes; all A records create an Internet route
options.B: Yes; an A record bypasses every NSG
options.C: No; because private names cannot contain A records
options.D: No; routing, security policy, and a service listener remain separate requirements

optionExplanations.A: DNS does not program an Internet route for each record.
optionExplanations.B: Name resolution cannot override network filtering.
optionExplanations.C: Private zones can host A records.
optionExplanations.D: DNS maps names to values but does not establish the full network path.

questions.stem: The web A record has ttl = 300. What does that mean?

options.A: DNS clients and resolvers may cache the record for 300 seconds according to its TTL
options.B: The target VM must remain running for exactly 300 minutes
options.C: Azure assigns 300 private IPs to the hostname
options.D: The DNS zone deletes itself after 300 queries

optionExplanations.A: TTL is a caching duration for the record set.
optionExplanations.B: There is no VM runtime timer here.
optionExplanations.C: TTL does not define record cardinality.
optionExplanations.D: TTL is not a query-count limit.

questions.stem: The record value is changed, but a client briefly returns the old address. What is a plausible explanation?

options.A: The Role tag forces the original IP forever
options.B: The old DNS answer may still be cached until its TTL expires
options.C: Terraform changed the VNet into a public DNS zone
options.D: The private zone copies the old VM disk contents

optionExplanations.A: Tags do not pin DNS answer caching.
optionExplanations.B: Inspect client and resolver caching before assuming the control-plane update failed.
optionExplanations.C: A record value update does not do that.
optionExplanations.D: DNS caches answers, not guest disks.

questions.stem: Would deleting an unrelated future VM automatically remove this explicitly declared web A record with autoregistration disabled?

options.A: Yes; Azure deletes every record whenever any VM is removed
options.B: Yes; /24 subnet membership controls all DNS record deletion
options.C: No; the record is managed explicitly rather than as that VM's autoregistered hostname
options.D: No; because A records can never be deleted

optionExplanations.A: That would not describe manually managed records.
optionExplanations.B: Subnet membership does not own this explicit record.
optionExplanations.C: Its lifecycle follows the configured DNS resource.
optionExplanations.D: They can be deleted through their management lifecycle.

questions.stem: The exercise adds app.clz.internal for an approved private IPv4. What record resource fits that goal?

options.A: Another A record named app in the existing private zone
options.B: A public load-balancing rule on TCP 80
options.C: A Role tag containing app.clz.internal
options.D: An outbound SNAT rule whose name is app

optionExplanations.A: The relative name and IPv4 value describe the intended mapping.
optionExplanations.B: That does not create the private DNS name.
optionExplanations.C: Tags do not define DNS records.
optionExplanations.D: SNAT resource names do not create DNS records.

questions.learningObjective: Keep Azure links distinct from peering
questions.stem: A second VNet is peered with the lesson VNet. Should private-zone resolution from the second VNet be assumed without DNS configuration?

options.A: Yes; peering automatically copies every private DNS link
options.B: Yes; matching subnet names guarantee DNS sharing
options.C: No; because peered VNets can never use private DNS
options.D: No; review private-zone links or a suitable forwarding/resolver path for the second VNet

optionExplanations.A: Do not assume private-zone links are inherited that way.
optionExplanations.B: Subnet names do not create resolution scope.
optionExplanations.C: They can use it with the appropriate design.
optionExplanations.D: Peering and name-resolution scope are different relationships.

questions.stem: An on-premises client needs to resolve the private zone. Which additional design is appropriate?

options.A: Publish the VM administrator password in the DNS record
options.B: Private connectivity plus conditional forwarding to an Azure DNS Private Resolver or approved DNS forwarder
options.C: Replace the A record's value with the whole VNet prefix
options.D: Rely on the ordinary Internet laptop's public resolver alone

optionExplanations.A: Passwords do not establish hybrid DNS forwarding.
optionExplanations.B: The hybrid client needs a reachable resolver path for the namespace.
optionExplanations.C: A prefix is not a valid single A-record address.
optionExplanations.D: The private zone is not publicly delegated to that resolver.

questions.stem: Why does the lesson choose an A record for web?

options.A: It maps the hostname to an IPv4 address
options.B: It aliases the hostname to another hostname
options.C: It specifies the preferred email server
options.D: It configures the TLS certificate authority

optionExplanations.A: The configured value is an IPv4 literal.
optionExplanations.B: That would describe a CNAME record.
optionExplanations.C: That would describe an MX record.
optionExplanations.D: That is not the function of an A record.

questions.learningObjective: Check the current zone link target
questions.stem: Which Terraform value ensures the private link refers to this lesson's VNet?

options.A: The name web-snet alone
options.B: The prior lesson's NAT public IP
options.C: azurerm_virtual_network.main.id
options.D: The Windows username from CLZ-210

optionExplanations.A: A subnet display name is not the VNet resource ID.
optionExplanations.B: An egress IP does not identify the linked VNet.
optionExplanations.C: The link's virtual_network_id uses that resource identity.
optionExplanations.D: Guest identity does not identify this DNS resolution scope.

questions.stem: An ordinary unconnected Internet laptop cannot resolve web.clz.internal while Azure CLI lists the record. What conclusion is reasonable?

options.A: The Azure record must be corrupt because all DNS is public
options.B: That client has no demonstrated private resolver path; the CLI result is still control-plane evidence
options.C: The laptop must run Terraform apply again without a plan
options.D: The NAT gateway output is guaranteed to repair name resolution

optionExplanations.A: Private DNS records are intentionally not globally public.
optionExplanations.B: Private DNS scope explains why those two observations can coexist.
optionExplanations.C: Reapplying does not provide the laptop with private resolver connectivity.
optionExplanations.D: NAT egress is not private-zone resolution scope.

questions.stem: Which observation demonstrates the lesson's intended name-resolution result?

options.A: A screenshot of the local terraform.tfvars.example file
options.B: A Terraform plan showing no proposed changes only
options.C: The homepage displays a DNS illustration
options.D: A linked-VNet client resolves web.clz.internal to 10.40.1.10

optionExplanations.A: That shows a source example, not a DNS response.
optionExplanations.B: That does not execute a client DNS query.
optionExplanations.C: A teaching diagram is not a live DNS test.
optionExplanations.D: The query exercises the actual resolver path and compares the expected value.

questions.learningObjective: Avoid treating resolution as service health
questions.stem: A linked client resolves the expected A record successfully. Which follow-up is needed before claiming a real application is healthy?

options.A: Nothing; any DNS answer proves HTTP 200
options.B: Test the actual service endpoint and its network permissions, if a workload is deployed
options.C: Only confirm the DNS TTL equals the port number
options.D: Only change the private zone to a different capitalization

optionExplanations.A: Address resolution does not run an HTTP health check.
optionExplanations.B: DNS success is only one part of application connectivity.
optionExplanations.C: TTL and service ports are unrelated.
optionExplanations.D: Naming case is not application health evidence.

questions.stem: Which production consideration belongs in selecting a private DNS namespace?

options.A: Use any existing production zone name without permission
options.B: Use the administrator password as the zone name
options.C: Assume every private namespace is visible only to its creator account
options.D: Avoid collisions with public and Active Directory namespaces and define ownership

optionExplanations.A: Unreviewed reuse can create conflicts.
optionExplanations.B: Namespace labels must not publish credentials.
optionExplanations.C: Resolution scope depends on network and resolver design, not that assumption.
optionExplanations.D: Name collisions and ambiguous authority can disrupt intended resolution.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret disabled registration with later VMs
questions.stem: A new VM is later deployed into the linked VNet. Does this lesson's disabled registration automatically create its hostname record?

options.A: Yes; any VNet link always enables registration
options.B: Yes; a Standard public IP creates its private hostname
options.C: No; explicitly manage its record or deliberately configure an appropriate registration design
options.D: No; because private zones cannot represent VM names

optionExplanations.A: The setting is explicitly false.
optionExplanations.B: A public IP is unrelated to private VM autoregistration.
optionExplanations.C: The current link is for resolution without automatic VM registration.
optionExplanations.D: They can represent them through manual or appropriate automatic records.

questions.stem: A client in the linked VNet uses Azure-provided DNS. Why is it an appropriate positive test location?

options.A: The resolver can consult private zones linked to that VNet
options.B: It bypasses every firewall between client and application
options.C: It converts private A records into public Internet routes
options.D: It automatically starts a web VM at 10.40.1.10

optionExplanations.A: The link connects the namespace to the client's resolution scope.
optionExplanations.B: DNS resolution does not bypass security policy.
optionExplanations.C: The answer remains an address value.
optionExplanations.D: The resolver does not create workloads.

questions.stem: Why should production DNS records follow service ownership rather than indefinite manual guesses?

options.A: DNS queries automatically correct every stale endpoint value
options.B: Terraform cannot manage DNS record resources
options.C: Private records cannot change after creation
options.D: Records must remain aligned with the actual endpoint lifecycle and address

optionExplanations.A: Resolvers do not infer the intended new address.
optionExplanations.B: The lesson explicitly manages one with Terraform.
optionExplanations.C: Their values can be updated through their resource lifecycle.
optionExplanations.D: Stale mappings can resolve successfully while directing clients incorrectly.

questions.stem: Does the CLZ-290 zone automatically link to CLZ-280's previously deployed VNet?

options.A: Yes; the sequential lesson ID automatically joins both VNets
options.B: Yes; a common environment tag merges the networks
options.C: No; the configuration links its own azurerm_virtual_network.main
options.D: No; because one zone can only ever link to one VNet

optionExplanations.A: Curriculum order does not create Azure relationships.
optionExplanations.B: Tags do not merge VNets.
optionExplanations.C: A new lesson does not implicitly change a separate deployment's DNS links.
optionExplanations.D: A zone can have multiple links when appropriately configured.

questions.stem: A client resolves web.clz.internal to an unexpected address after an environment change. What should be examined?

options.A: The active resolver path, zone authority, record value, and cached answers
options.B: Only the VM's administrator password
options.C: Only the public IP's SKU
options.D: Only the quiz question ID

optionExplanations.A: These identify which DNS data the client is actually using.
optionExplanations.B: Credentials do not reveal DNS authority.
optionExplanations.C: No public IP controls this literal private A-record value.
optionExplanations.D: Assessment identifiers are not resolver configuration.

questions.stem: Which CLZ-290 resource contributes DNS-service cost even though no VM is deployed?

options.A: Only the local PowerShell Resolve-DnsName command itself
options.B: The Private DNS zone and its query usage
options.C: The numerical value 10.40.1.10 as a standalone hourly resource
options.D: The Markdown navigation link

optionExplanations.A: A local command is not the Azure hosted zone charge.
optionExplanations.B: The lesson's DNS service can be billable without compute.
optionExplanations.C: The record's address literal is not a provisioned VM or IP resource.
optionExplanations.D: A documentation link has no Azure DNS hourly charge.

questions.stem: Before applying a change to the web A-record value, what does Terraform plan help the learner inspect?

options.A: Every cached answer on every client
options.B: The service's HTTP response before a workload exists
options.C: The intended record update and other proposed resource changes
options.D: The Windows password of a VM at the illustrative address

optionExplanations.A: Terraform cannot list all clients' DNS caches.
optionExplanations.B: A plan does not create or test an undeployed application.
optionExplanations.C: Planning is a nonapplying review of the desired infrastructure change.
optionExplanations.D: The lesson creates no such VM.

questions.stem: What should the managed cleanup remove from CLZ-290?

options.A: Only the cached answer on the learner's laptop
options.B: The private zone, VNet link, explicit A record, and lesson network
options.C: Only the record's TTL while keeping the zone forever
options.D: Only the web application at 10.40.1.10

optionExplanations.A: Clearing a client cache does not delete Azure resources.
optionExplanations.B: Destroy should remove the configured DNS and supporting lab resources.
optionExplanations.C: That is not full managed teardown.
optionExplanations.D: No application exists there in the unmodified lesson.

questions.stem: Which final verification matches the documented cleanup after destroy?

options.A: A laptop still returns a cached DNS answer
options.B: terraform fmt reports no changes
options.C: An Internet lookup times out for a private zone
options.D: az group exists returns false for the resource-group name captured before deletion

optionExplanations.A: Caches can persist briefly and do not prove current Azure resources exist.
optionExplanations.B: Formatting is unrelated to cloud absence.
optionExplanations.C: That could occur before cleanup and is not sufficient evidence.
optionExplanations.D: It confirms absence of the intended managed group.
